questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of the following is a fruit?
questions.explanation: A mango is the fruit of the mango tree.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which bird commonly gives us eggs for food?
questions.explanation: Hens are reared for eggs.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which group has only herbivores?
questions.explanation: Cow, goat and deer eat only plants.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these is mainly eaten for its leaves?
questions.explanation: Cabbage is a bunch of leaves.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Rani says honey is a plant food because bees collect it from flowers. Which reply is correct?
options: Honey is an animal product because bees make it from nectar
questions.explanation: Bees collect nectar and turn it into honey in their hives, so honey is made by an animal.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: What are cereals and pulses? Give two examples of each.
questions.answer: Cereals are grains that give mainly carbohydrates, e.g. wheat and rice. Pulses are seeds rich in protein, e.g. moong and gram.
questions.explanation: Cereals and pulses are staple foods.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Why are humans called omnivores?
questions.answer: Humans can eat both plant foods such as vegetables and cereals and animal foods such as milk, eggs and meat.
questions.explanation: Omnivores feed on both plants and animals.

questions.q: Which food gives us roughage?
questions.explanation: Vegetables, fruits and whole grains are rich in fibre.

questions.q: A disease caused by long-term lack of a nutrient is called a
questions.explanation: Deficiency diseases occur when the diet lacks some nutrient.

questions.q: Our skin makes vitamin D when exposed to
questions.explanation: Sunlight helps the skin to make vitamin D.

questions.q: A food gives a violet colour when copper sulphate and caustic soda solutions are added. It contains
questions.explanation: A violet colour shows the presence of protein.

questions.q: In some hilly regions, many people have goitre. Which change in diet would help?
questions.explanation: Iodised salt supplies iodine, preventing goitre.

questions.q: Why do we need roughage though it gives no nutrients?
questions.answer: Roughage adds bulk, helps move food through the gut and removes undigested waste, preventing constipation.
questions.explanation: Fibre helps the body get rid of undigested food.

questions.q: A raw potato and a piece of paneer are tested with iodine solution. What result do you expect and why?
questions.answer: The potato turns blue-black as it contains starch. The paneer does not change colour as it has mostly protein and fat, with no starch.
questions.explanation: Iodine tests only for starch.

questions.q: Coir is obtained from the
questions.explanation: Coir fibre is obtained from the outer covering of coconut.

questions.q: Which animal gives hair that is made into woollen yarn in hills?
questions.explanation: Yak hair is used for wool in hill regions.

questions.q: In weaving, two sets of yarn are arranged
options: At right angles to each other
questions.explanation: Warp and weft yarns cross at right angles.

questions.q: The cotton boll is the
questions.explanation: The boll is the fruit that bursts open to show cotton fibres.

questions.q: Which sequence for silk is correct?
questions.explanation: The silk thread is unwound from the cocoon, turned into yarn and woven into cloth.

questions.q: What is shearing? Does it harm the sheep?
questions.answer: Shearing is removing the fleece of the sheep by cutting. It does not hurt the sheep since the hair is cut like our hair.
questions.explanation: The wool is then cleaned and spun.

questions.q: Coir is used for doormats and ropes. Which property of coir makes this suitable?
questions.answer: Coir fibre is coarse and strong, so it can scrub dirt and bear pulling.
questions.explanation: The use of a fibre depends on its properties.

questions.q: Metals generally have a shine, which is known as
questions.explanation: Shining surface is called lustre.

questions.q: Which of these is rough to touch?
questions.explanation: Sandpaper has a rough surface.

questions.q: Which of the following is translucent?
questions.explanation: Butter paper allows light but you cannot see clearly through it.

questions.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Each object is made of only one material
A chair can only be wood
An object can be made of more than one material
questions.explanation: A chair can have a metal frame and a plastic seat, for example.

questions.q: A raincoat is made of plastic or rubber-coated cloth because
options: Water does not pass through them easily
questions.explanation: Waterproof materials keep the body dry.

questions.q: What is lustre? Name two materials that show lustre.
questions.answer: Lustre is the shining appearance of a surface. Metals such as gold and silver show it.
questions.explanation: Lustre is a property of many metals.

questions.q: Why are different materials used to make different objects? Give an example.
questions.answer: Materials have different properties, so we pick the one that suits the use. For example, glass is used for windows as it is transparent, and iron for tools as it is hard.
questions.explanation: Properties decide use.

questions.q: A mixture is
options: Two or more substances mixed together
questions.explanation: A mixture contains more than one substance.

questions.q: Sieving is used when the components of a mixture are of
questions.explanation: Smaller particles pass through while larger remain.

questions.q: Husk is separated from rice grains by
questions.explanation: Wind blows away the light husk.

questions.q: Which method can separate sand from water?
questions.explanation: Filter paper holds back the sand.

questions.q: Which two steps together separate a mixture of sand and water without special tools?
questions.explanation: Sand settles and the clear water is poured off.

questions.q: Why is sieving useful? Give an example.
questions.answer: It separates particles of different sizes, such as flour from bran or sand from gravel.
questions.explanation: Sieves are used at home and on farms.

questions.q: A mixture of rice and small gravel is given. Which method would you use and why?
questions.answer: Handpicking, because the gravel pieces are visible and the quantity is small. A sieve could also be used if the sizes differ enough.
keyPoints: Reason linked to visibility or size
questions.explanation: Choose the method to suit the mixture.

questions.q: A change that can be undone is called a
questions.explanation: Reversible changes can be changed back.

questions.q: Rust on iron is
questions.explanation: Rust is a reddish-brown flaky coating.

questions.q: Tearing a sheet of paper into pieces is
questions.explanation: Torn pieces cannot be made into the original sheet.

questions.q: Which of the following is reversible?
options: Folding and unfolding a sheet of paper
questions.explanation: The paper can be folded and unfolded again.

questions.q: Water drops form on the inside of a lid covering a pan of boiling water. This shows
questions.explanation: Vapour cools on the lid and turns to liquid.

questions.q: What is rusting? State what is needed for it.
questions.answer: Rusting is the formation of a reddish-brown layer on iron when it is exposed to air and moisture.
questions.explanation: Rust weakens iron.

questions.q: Is dissolving sugar in water a reversible change? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes, sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water, so the change can be reversed.
questions.explanation: No new substance is made.

questions.q: Mint is a
questions.explanation: Mint is a small plant with a soft green stem.

questions.q: Which part of the plant holds it in the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant.

questions.q: Transpiration helps the plant by
options: Removing excess water and cooling the plant
questions.explanation: Water vapour lost through stomata cools the plant and helps water rise.

questions.q: Food in plants is mainly made in the
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and do photosynthesis.

questions.q: A potted plant is covered with a clear polythene bag and kept in sunlight. After some time water drops appear inside the bag. This is due to
questions.explanation: Water vapour lost by the leaves condenses inside the bag.

questions.q: Name three types of plants based on their stems and give one example for each.
questions.explanation: Stem size and nature are used to classify plants.

questions.q: How does a flower help a plant to produce seeds?
questions.answer: Pollen from the stamen reaches the pistil, fertilisation takes place and the ovules develop into seeds while the ovary becomes the fruit.
questions.explanation: Flowers are reproductive parts.

questions.q: The place where two bones meet is called a
questions.explanation: Bones are connected at joints.

questions.q: The tip of the nose can be bent because it has
questions.explanation: Cartilage is flexible.

questions.q: The leg can bend backward at the knee but not forward because the knee is a
questions.explanation: A hinge joint moves in only one direction.

questions.q: The backbone is made up of many small bones, which allows us to
questions.explanation: Many small bones with joints between them permit bending.

questions.q: If the knee joint of a person became fixed, what would be most affected?
questions.explanation: Walking and bending the leg need a movable knee.

questions.q: Explain how a snail moves.
questions.answer: A snail has a muscular foot. It glides forward on a slimy layer by waves of muscle movement.
questions.explanation: Snails have no limbs.

questions.q: Why can we not bend our elbow backwards?
questions.answer: The elbow is a hinge joint, which allows movement in only one direction.
questions.explanation: Joint structure decides range of movement.

questions.q: A fish lives in
questions.explanation: Fish live in water.

questions.q: Which of these is a characteristic of living things?
options: They stay the same size forever
questions.explanation: Growth is a feature of living things.

questions.q: The leaves of the touch-me-not plant fold when touched. This shows that plants
questions.explanation: Response to touch is a response to a stimulus.

questions.q: Yaks living in cold mountain regions have
questions.explanation: A thick coat protects them from cold.

questions.q: Which is an adaptation of desert plants?
options: Waxy coating on stems that reduces water loss
questions.explanation: A waxy covering reduces loss of water.

questions.q: What is adaptation? Give one example from a bird or an animal.
questions.answer: Adaptation is a special feature that helps an organism live in its habitat. For example, a fish has gills to breathe in water.
questions.explanation: Adaptations help survival.

questions.q: Why can a polar bear not live in a hot desert?
questions.answer: Its thick fur and fat suit cold regions; in a hot desert it would overheat and would not find the food it eats.
questions.explanation: Organisms are adapted to specific habitats.

questions.q: Motion means a change in
questions.explanation: An object moves when its position changes with time.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the length of a book?
questions.explanation: A scale measures length.

questions.q: 5 km is equal to
The motion of a car on a straight road is called
questions.explanation: Straight-line motion is rectilinear.

questions.q: A person sits in a moving train and says her seat is not moving. Which is a correct view?
options: The seat is not at rest in any way
Rest and motion are the same
The seat is at rest compared to her but moving compared to the ground
questions.explanation: Rest and motion depend on the observer or reference.

questions.q: Name three types of motion with an example of each.
questions.answer: Rectilinear: a car on a straight road. Circular: a stone whirled on a string. Periodic: a swing.
questions.explanation: Motion is classified by path.

questions.q: Two children measure the length of a desk by their foot lengths and get different numbers. Explain and suggest a solution.
questions.answer: Their feet are different sizes, so the numbers differ. They should use a standard unit such as the metre scale.
questions.explanation: Standard units give uniform results.

questions.q: Which of these is a source of light?
questions.explanation: An electric bulb gives its own light.

questions.q: Opaque objects
options: Allow no light to pass through
questions.explanation: They block light.

questions.q: The shadow of an object is sharpest when the light source is
questions.explanation: A small bright source gives a well-defined shadow.

questions.q: In a pinhole camera the hole should be
questions.explanation: A small hole gives a clearer image.

questions.q: The Moon appears bright at night because
options: It reflects light from the Sun
It is a mirror made by people
questions.explanation: The Moon is non-luminous and reflects sunlight.

questions.q: Differentiate luminous and non-luminous objects with examples.
questions.answer: Luminous objects give out their own light, such as the Sun. Non-luminous objects do not, such as a table.
questions.explanation: We see non-luminous objects by reflected light.

questions.q: Why are shadows shortest around noon?
questions.answer: At noon the Sun is almost overhead, so light falls nearly straight down and shadows are short.
questions.explanation: Shadow length depends on the Sun's height.

questions.q: Electric current flows only in a
questions.explanation: A complete path is needed.

questions.q: A battery is
questions.explanation: Cells together form a battery.

questions.q: The glass of a bulb
options: Does not allow current to pass but allows light
questions.explanation: Glass is an insulator and transparent.

questions.q: For experiments in school, which source of electricity should never be used?
questions.explanation: Mains electricity can cause serious shocks.

questions.q: In a circuit, a student uses an iron nail instead of a switch to close the gap. What happens?
options: The bulb lights because iron is a conductor
questions.explanation: The nail is a conductor and completes the circuit.

questions.q: Why does a bulb not glow when the circuit has a gap?
questions.answer: The gap breaks the path, so no electric current flows to the filament.
questions.explanation: A complete path is needed for current.

questions.q: Why are cells used for experiments rather than the electricity from the wall socket?
questions.answer: Cells give a small, safe voltage, but mains electricity can cause fatal electric shocks.
questions.explanation: Safety matters in experiments.

questions.q: Magnets attract
questions.explanation: Only some materials are magnetic.

questions.q: A compass is used to find
questions.explanation: It points north-south.

questions.q: Old sailors used a magnetic needle on the sea to
questions.explanation: The needle points north-south, helping them navigate.

questions.q: If you cut a bar magnet in two, can you get a piece with only a north pole?
options: No, each piece has two poles
Yes, if cut at the middle
questions.explanation: Poles cannot be separated.

questions.q: A bar magnet is placed on a floating piece of cork in a bowl of water. It turns and settles. In which direction does it point?
questions.explanation: A free magnet aligns north-south.

questions.q: Name three magnetic and three non-magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Magnetic: iron, nickel, cobalt. Non-magnetic: wood, plastic, rubber.
questions.explanation: Only iron, nickel and cobalt and their alloys are magnetic.

questions.q: How can you show that like poles repel?
questions.answer: Hang a bar magnet freely and bring the north pole of another magnet close to its north pole. The hanging magnet is pushed away.
questions.explanation: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
